title: Death Rate per 1,000 per Annum among Resident Foreign Community, 1902–1916
caption_extra: Boxed table headed 'Death Rate per 1,000 per Annum among Resident Foreign Community'. A vertical note alongside the 1910–1916 rows reads 'septic tanks introduced 1910' (transcribed as a note, not a column).
footnotes: These figures show that neither in the general death rate, nor in the death rate for typhoid fever, which is the recognised index of water-borne disease through faecal contamination, is there any appreciable sign of danger resulting from the use of septic tanks in the French Concession during recent years.

title: Average of Data of Monthly Analyses of Shanghai Waterworks Company's Water

columns: Organisms of Coli group present in c.c.

footnotes: These figures show:
(1) That Whangpoo River water has been and remains a water of remarkable chemical purity.

(2) That the self-purification naturally effected by the big volume of water which flows down the Whangpoo and the purification subsequently effected at the Waterworks is such as to effectively deal with the increasing quantity of domestic sewage contamination which the great increase in population must have given rise to.

(3) That as no progressive deterioration in chemical purity is shown it may safely be concluded that there is a very considerable margin of safety, that is to say, the Whangpoo River is able to self-purify a very considerable addition of sewage contamination.
(4) No progressive increase of bacterial contamination.
